about.title: Chowchilla Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Chowchilla's economy runs on agriculture, distribution, and the correctional facilities nearby, all of which carry real injury risk from heavy equipment, repetitive strain, and vehicle traffic. When a workplace injury happens, most employees assume workers' compensation is their only path forward, but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system entirely. This matters in a town where flatbed trucks, delivery vans, and farm vehicles regularly move along Robertson Boulevard and Trinity Avenue near work sites. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results, we simply connect injured workers with an independent attorney, at no cost to you, who can review your specific situation and explain whether a third-party claim applies alongside your workers' comp benefits. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless the attorney recovers something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Independent Attorney First

items.title: Workers' Comp Isn't Always the Whole Story
items.desc: California treats workers' comp as the exclusive remedy against your employer in most cases, but a negligent third party, like a subcontractor or equipment maker, can still be held separately liable.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a workplace injury to your employer, and missing that window can complicate your benefits, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Retaliation Is Illegal, and Deadlines Still Apply
items.desc: Your employer cannot legally punish you for reporting an injury, and if a third-party claim exists, California gives you two years to pursue it, so understanding your timeline early protects your options.

items.question: I was hurt at a job site near SR-99, does workers' comp cover everything?
items.answer: Workers' comp usually covers medical costs and lost wages regardless of fault, but it typically doesn't cover pain and suffering. If a third party, like a delivery driver or equipment supplier, contributed to the crash or incident, a separate claim may be available alongside your workers' comp benefits.

items.question: What if my employer discourages me from reporting my injury?
items.answer: Retaliation for reporting a workplace injury is illegal in California. If you're facing pressure not to report, an independent attorney can advise you on protecting your rights while still meeting the 30-day reporting window.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, the connection service itself is free, and LawProactive is not a law firm. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover something for you.
